euclid.name: Euclid of Alexandria
euclid.role: Alexandrian Geometer; Author of the Elements
euclid.bio: Formulated division in extreme and mean ratio in Elements Book II Proposition 11 and Book VI Proposition 30, applying it to construct the regular pentagon (IV.11) and the icosahedron and dodecahedron (Book XIII).

claudius-ptolemy.name: Claudius Ptolemy
claudius-ptolemy.bio: Introduced the streamlined circle-and-midpoint construction of the regular decagon and pentagon in Almagest Book I, Chapter 10 to compute his trigonometric table of chords.

luca-pacioli.name: Luca Pacioli
luca-pacioli.role: Franciscan Mathematician; Author of De Divina Proportione (1509)
luca-pacioli.bio: Chronicled thirteen 'effects' of extreme and mean ratio in De Divina Proportione (1509, illustrated by Leonardo da Vinci), popularizing the Renaissance title Divina Proportione.

johannes-kepler.name: Johannes Kepler
johannes-kepler.bio: Described the Pythagorean theorem and division in extreme and mean ratio as the 'two great treasures of geometry' (1597 letter to Michael Mästlin) and studied the 1 : √φ : φ right triangle and rhombic triacontahedron.

william-hooper.name: William Hooper
william-hooper.bio: Published the earliest known geometric missing-area rectangle dissection fallacy in Rational Recreations (1774/1794), whose vanishing-gap limit is governed by φ.

emile-lemoine.name: Émile Michel Hyacinthe Lemoine
emile-lemoine.bio: Founded Géométrographie (1902), a quantitative operational calculus measuring the simplicity and exactitude of ruler-and-compass constructions, and recorded early minimal divisions in extreme and mean ratio.

paul-curry.name: Paul Curry
paul-curry.bio: Invented the Curry Paradox (1953) of area-discrepant triangle and rectangle rearrangements driven by Fibonacci slopes approaching 1/φ.

h-e-huntley.name: H. E. Huntley
h-e-huntley.bio: Author of The Divine Proportion: A Study in Mathematical Beauty (Dover, 1970), highlighting unexpected appearances of φ such as the angle-bisector circle in the 3-4-5 right triangle.

h-s-m-coxeter.name: H. S. M. Coxeter
h-s-m-coxeter.bio: Communicated George Odom's equilateral midline golden-section problem in the American Mathematical Monthly (Problem E3007, 1983) and championed classical synthetic and projective geometry.

george-odom.name: George Odom
george-odom.bio: Discovered the celebrated two-line equilateral-triangle midline construction of φ (1982–1983) through visual exploration of polyhedra and three-dimensional models.

alexander-bogomolny.name: Alexander Bogomolny
alexander-bogomolny.bio: Founded Interactive Mathematics Miscellany and Puzzles (Cut-the-Knot, 1996–2018), curating, proving, and illustrating dozens of classical and contemporary Golden Ratio constructions contributed by geometers worldwide.

ron-knott.name: Ron Knott
ron-knott.bio: Creator of the encyclopedic Fibonacci Numbers and the Golden Section resource (cataloged in sibling repository geometor/knott).

v-v-prasolov.name: Viktor Vasil'evich Prasolov
v-v-prasolov.role: Russian Geometer & Author; Independent University of Moscow
v-v-prasolov.bio: Author of Problems in Plane and Solid Geometry, documenting affine equi-area characterizations of golden diagonal ratios in general convex pentagons.

alexandre-borovik.name: Alexandre Borovik
alexandre-borovik.bio: Observed the golden rectangle embedded inside Bùi Quang Tuân's concentric Greek cross and square configuration on Cut-the-Knot.

jerzy-kocik.name: Jerzy Kocik
jerzy-kocik.bio: Discovered and analyzed the Apollonian 'Golden Window' circle packing (Mathematics Magazine, 2010), showing how simultaneous tangency forces powers of φ.

jingcheng-tong.name: Jingcheng Tong
jingcheng-tong.bio: Characterized area-bisecting chords in trapezoids whose parallel bases stand in ratio 1 : 3, dividing both legs in the golden ratio.

jo-niemeyer.name: Jo Niemeyer
jo-niemeyer.bio: Constructivist artist whose sculptures and geometric studies feature the golden division generated by three equal leaning segments.

kurt-hofstetter.name: Kurt Hofstetter
kurt-hofstetter.bio: Published a remarkable series of minimal 5-step Euclidean, 5-circle Mascheroni compass-only, and fixed-opening rusty-compass Golden Ratio constructions in Forum Geometricorum (2002–2005).

michel-bataille.name: Michel Bataille
michel-bataille.bio: Prolific contributor to Crux Mathematicorum and Forum Geometricorum; devised the equilateral-triangle-and-square radical-axis construction of φ (2011).

bui-quang-tuan.name: Bùi Quang Tuân
bui-quang-tuan.bio: Discovered numerous synthetic Golden Ratio theorems curated on Cut-the-Knot, including a 5-step collinear circle construction, the Greek Cross & Square, Four Golden Circles, Van Obel isosceles division, and infinite circle-secant families.

tran-quang-hung.name: Tran Quang Hung
tran-quang-hung.role: Vietnamese Geometer; Hanoi University of Science High School
tran-quang-hung.bio: Contributed an extraordinary suite of synthetic Golden Ratio discoveries across equilateral triangles, squares, 3×3 grids, hexagons, pentagon stars, Wu Xing rotations, rhombi, trapezoids, and mixtilinear circles.

dao-thanh-oai.name: Dao Thanh Oai
dao-thanh-oai.bio: Known for discoveries in Euclidean and projective triangle/polygon geometry, including the regular-pentagon edge-perpendicular division in φ.

nguyen-thanh-dung.name: Nguyen Thanh Dung
nguyen-thanh-dung.bio: Contributed butterfly-chord equilateral constructions and 2×2 square lattice divisions in extreme and mean ratio on Cut-the-Knot.

quang-duong.name: Quang Duong
quang-duong.bio: Contributed synthetic proofs for Tran Quang Hung's reflected equilateral and incircle Golden Ratio theorems.

gregoire-nicollier.name: Grégoire Nicollier
gregoire-nicollier.role: Swiss Mathematician; University of Applied Sciences of Western Switzerland
gregoire-nicollier.bio: Contributed analytic and synthetic proofs of polygonal and equilateral Golden Ratio configurations on Cut-the-Knot.

leo-giugiuc.name: Leonard Giugiuc
leo-giugiuc.bio: Co-solved and generalized several trigonometric, mixtilinear, and butterfly Golden Ratio problems curated by Alexander Bogomolny.

ercole-suppa.name: Ercole Suppa
ercole-suppa.bio: Researcher in triangle centers and sangaku-style circle configurations; discovered the golden ratio of inradii in a midpoint-partitioned square (2015).

elliot-mcgucken.name: Elliot McGucken
elliot-mcgucken.bio: Contributed golden-section constructions in two and three tangent equal circles and 3×3 square grids on Cut-the-Knot.

thanos-kalogerakis.name: Thanos Kalogerakis
thanos-kalogerakis.bio: Observed the diameter-to-secant golden ratio across two externally tangent equal circles.

john-arioni.name: John Arioni
john-arioni.bio: Contributed the Yin-Yang twin-circle secant construction and the 30°-rotated unit square diagonal-circle construction of φ on Cut-the-Knot.

john-molokach.name: John Molokach
john-molokach.bio: Devised the construction of a golden rhombus and consecutive powers of φ from two unit-shifted 1×3 rectangles and an inscribed unit circle.
